name: rqlite
tagline: Lightweight distributed database that replicates SQLite over Raft behind a simple HTTP API.
description: rqlite turns SQLite into a fault-tolerant, highly available cluster: a single Go binary runs Raft consensus and applies every write to a local SQLite database on each node. Clients talk to it over a JSON HTTP API (or a Go/Python/JS client) and can choose read consistency levels from fast local reads to fully linearizable ones. It adds hot backups to S3, change data capture streams, SQLite extension loading (for example sqlite-vec) and Kubernetes-friendly auto-clustering. It is a pragmatic choice for small, critical datasets such as control-plane state, not a scale-out database: all data must fit on every node and writes go through one leader.

scale.notes: Typically 3-5 voting nodes plus optional read-only nodes; every node holds the full dataset and writes go through the Raft leader.

strengths: One binary, no dependencies: easiest way to make SQLite highly available
Per-request read consistency: none, weak, linearizable
Automatic S3/GCS backups and restore from plain SQLite files
Change data capture to stream writes elsewhere
Load SQLite extensions such as sqlite-vec for vector search
weaknesses: Write throughput limited to one Raft leader and disk fsync speed
No interactive multi-statement transactions; only batched requests are atomic
Non-deterministic SQL functions need care under replication
Full dataset must fit on every node
useCases: Control-plane and configuration state for distributed systems
Small HA databases at the edge or in IoT gateways
Service metadata where SQLite simplicity is wanted with failover
notIdealFor: Datasets larger than a single node
